creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A Codex agent cannot report its own state from its shell tool: the daemon refuses it as a nested agent. `"$MUSTER_DAEMON" report --waiting ""` exited 1: "pane

runs codex, and this report came from another codex (pid N), outside the process group the pane's own agent runs in; it inherited the pane's environment, and its reports are not the pane's". `muster msg join` from the same tool call succeeded, and `muster window` still showed the Codex adapter's own reports. ## Measured: muster 0.13.0, 2026-10-05, devenv Seen twice, in two reviewer panes of one council. Codex ran the command through its exec tool (`exec_command`). Inferred, not checked: the process that runs Codex's commands is itself a codex process in a process group of its own, so the attribution added for a_2XssfzCUV reads it as a nested agent. That answers a_2bit9y3Xw for Codex on Linux: its shell tool does leave the agent's process group. ## Why it matters The SessionStart line tells every agent, Codex included, to run this command before ending a turn to wait. A Codex agent that follows it gets an error, and its wait is never declared. ## Things that might be true - **Take a report whose nearest codex ancestor sits directly below the pane's codex as the pane's own.** - Or drop the report line from the Codex SessionStart hook until a Codex agent can report, and say in `muster docs limits` that it cannot.
title: 🚫 A Codex agent's own report --waiting is refused as a nested codex
